mainEntity.name: How long does a home kitchen addition take from start to finish?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen addition generally takes several months to complete, typically ranging from three to six months depending on size, site preparation, and material availability. The pre-construction phase involves drafting blueprints, structural calculations, and municipal permit processing. Once ground breaks, foundation work, framing, and mechanical inspections require sequential sign-offs before drywall, cabinetry, and tile can proceed. Delays can happen if custom cabinetry requires extended lead times or if foundation excavation reveals buried obstacles.
acceptedAnswer.description: Kitchen additions usually take three to six months from groundbreaking through final inspection, influenced by permitting, inspections, and custom material lead times.
